description:
A team with a simple vision - to learn better and communicate better.

Our universe is ever-expanding, and so is knowledge. To understand it better, we need a medium that connects with people. For us, that medium is storytelling, because it reaches both the mind and the heart.

Our goal is to simplify complex space concepts so that everyone can understand them. With a little passion and a lot of effort, we are working towards making space learning universal.
summary:
Our team is addressing the challenge: Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.
Our first step was to learn more about NASA's historic missions that mark the achievements of all humanity. We aimed to understand their purposes, scientific contributions, discoveries, and ultimate fate. 
There, we realised that every piece of hardware left behind has a story to tell. So, we chose to present their experiences through the object's own point of view, giving these forgotten pieces of technology a voice.
To understand the space concepts and know the universe better, we need a medium, and storytelling is the best way to reach both the mind and the heart.
Hence, our team GDGH_Silent Telemetry presents a digital science storybook with an aim to make space science universal. A little passion and greater effort fuel us in this mission.
details:
Our project is a digital science storybook titled “Abandoned but not Forgotten”. It tells the stories of NASA's equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars — not from a human's point of view, but from the object's own point of view, including the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage, the Lunar Retroreflector, and the Opportunity Rover

The reader opens the storybook and meets each piece of equipment as a character. Each chapter follows one object through its mission — its launch, its purpose, its scientific discoveries, and its final moments. Simple language, visuals, and storytelling make complex space concepts easy to understand for students, children, and the general public.

It makes space science simple, interesting, and emotional. Instead of reading only facts and dates, readers connect with the machines as if they were heroes. This helps in better learning, better memory, and more curiosity about space.

Our aim is to make space science universal. We want young learners, especially those without a science background, to understand NASA's missions and feel inspired by them. It also honours the forgotten machines that contributed to humanity's achievements.

We used research from NASA's official mission pages and archives, and developed the storybook as a digital interactive book using web tools for design, illustration, and storytelling.

The creativity lies in giving a voice to forgotten technology. Instead of a textbook style, we used first-person storytelling, emotions, and imagination, while keeping the science accurate.

We considered scientific accuracy, simple language, age-friendly storytelling, emotional connection, and easy access for all learners. We also ensured that the stories respect the real history of each mission.
